mergeRequest.title: Add label filters to the issue list
mergeRequest.description: Adds a filter bar above the issue list, with one filter per label plus All, and a count of open issues in the header. The new behaviour has unit tests in App.spec.js.

issue.title: Filter issues by label
requirements: Show one filter per label, plus All.
Selecting a label shows the open issues with that label, without loading the list again.
Show how many open issues match the selected label, as "1 open issue" or "2 open issues".
Cover the filter with unit tests.

sampleReview.summary: Request changes. One thing blocks the merge: every label click loads the whole list again, and the page loads it twice on start, which the issue rules out and which blanks the list on each click. Must fix before merging: the count ignores the filter, the filters cannot be used from a keyboard, a failed request now leaves the page loading forever, the new grid overflows a phone, and the first spec cannot fail. Keep visibleIssues: filtering the loaded list in a computed is the right shape, so the main fix is deleting the watch.

comments.title: Every label click loads the list again
comments.body: The watch runs loadIssues on every label change, and immediate: true runs it on start next to onMounted, so the page sends two requests on load and one per click, and the list blanks to Loading issues… each time. The issue asks for filtering without a reload, and visibleIssues already filters the loaded issues: delete the watch and keep onMounted(loadIssues). If the server ever has to filter, send the label with the request and ignore a response for a label that is no longer selected.

comments.title: The count ignores the selected label
comments.body: openCount counts every open issue, so the header says 5 open issues while the bug filter shows 2, and a single match would read 1 open issues. Count visibleIssues instead and choose issue or issues from the number.

comments.title: The filters are spans, so a keyboard cannot use them
comments.body: A span with a click handler cannot take focus or be pressed with Enter or Space, and nothing tells a screen reader which filter is on: the active class only changes the colour. Use <button type="button"> with :aria-pressed, and add the :key this v-for is missing. The h3 above them also skips a heading level; a plain label for the group is enough.

comments.title: A ul can only hold li elements
comments.body: The change swapped the li for a div inside the ul. Browsers still draw it, but the HTML is invalid and screen readers stop announcing a list of five items. Keep the li from main.

comments.title: A failed request now leaves the page loading
comments.body: main wrapped the request in try, catch and finally. Without them, a rejected request leaves loading true forever, never shows the error and ends as an unhandled rejection. Put them back, and give the error state a Try again button while you are there.

comments.title: Fixed columns overflow a phone
comments.body: Three fixed columns need about 664px, so on a 360px phone every row scrolls sideways and long titles cannot wrap. Give the title minmax(0, 1fr) and drop to one column on narrow screens. Check it in the preview at 360px: the checks here do not measure layout.

comments.title: The filter bar cannot wrap
comments.body: With nowrap and no flex-wrap, the four filters and their heading run past the card on a phone. Let the bar wrap.

comments.title: This test passes without checking anything
comments.body: The assertion sits in a setTimeout that fires after the test has returned, so Jest reports a pass even if no issue renders. Make the test async, use fake timers or mock the request, await flushPromises() and then assert on what renders.

comments.title: The filter test reads internal state
comments.body: Checking selectedLabel passes even when the list is wrong or reloads. After the click, assert on the rendered titles and the count, and that the loading text does not come back: that is the regression this change introduced.
